# Research report: are the product manager and product owner one role, and what a second role serves

## Executive summary

*How to read the labels.* Each finding carries a confidence: **high** —
several sources opened in full agree, at least one primary (the author,
framework, or standard itself); **medium** — one opened source, or
secondary accounts only; **low** — recall without a source, or a primary
that could not be read. "Secondhand" marks a quote carried by a secondary
account because the primary was unreachable. Confidence is about the
evidence; where a finding predicts an outcome, likelihood is stated in
its own phrase.

*How the sources' vocabulary maps to the shop.* "One person" in the
sources means one accountable party; in this shop a role is a named
capability contract assigned by process steps to whoever fills it, so
"one person" reads as "one accountability". `lead-pm` runs in the
authority's own turn (the interactive position); `lead-po` runs as a
delegated subagent (the batch position). SAFe is the Scaled Agile
Framework; it is cited here as one position on the spectrum, not as a
model for the shop. The prior report on these roles is
`research:research/pm-po-roles-2026-08`.

1. **Cagan's objection is to two accountabilities and to mediated access,
   not to a second role as such.** His test is "so long as it was one
   person"; the harm he names is that the split "causes the PM to lose
   the direct access to engineers" and that "there is no clear owner". He
   sanctions offloading work — acceptance testing is "a very minor
   responsibility", research logistics can go to "part-time
   administrative help" — and accepts a separately-scoped role beside the
   PM (the business owner) when its responsibilities are explicit and it
   does not own solutions. *(High — five SVPG essays opened in full.)*
2. **The Scrum Guide, Pichler, Scrum.org, LeSS, and Perri converge on
   the same shape: one non-delegable accountability, delegable work.**
   Scrum Guide 2020: "The Product Owner may do the above work or may
   delegate the responsibility to others. Regardless, the Product Owner
   remains accountable"; "one person, not a committee". Perri: "Product
   Owner is a role you play on a Scrum team. Product Manager is the
   job." Cagan (interview): "The role the product manager plays on an
   Agile team is the product owner role." Pichler disagrees with Cagan on
   which name carries the larger scope but agrees on one accountability.
   *(High.)*
3. **The answer to "same role with different activities?" is: in the
   sources' own vocabulary, yes — and the distinction they draw is
   accountability versus responsibility, not role versus activity.** The
   2020 Scrum Guide replaced "role" with "accountability" — Milner's
   commentary reads the change as separating role from job title
   ("Apparently some people thought that the term 'role' meant job
   title"); the Guide's own revisions page gives no rationale, and its
   authors cite removing the separate Development Team; ISO/IEC/IEEE 24765
   defines a role (its second definition, credited to the PMBOK Guide
   4th ed.) as "a defined function to be performed by a project team member"
   and puts activities and tasks in processes; Holacracy's role form is
   purpose + exclusive domain + accountabilities, where accountabilities
   are "ongoing activities". Under every one of these forms, "one role
   with several activities" is the default, and a second role has to earn
   its existence. *(High.)*
4. **The case for two roles, at its strongest, rests on scale and
   distribution — and the reported consequence of that split is a
   hollowed-out PO.** The two-role case: SAFe ("a single person cannot
   handle product and market strategy while also being dedicated to
   agile teams" — secondhand, SAFe's pages are login-walled); Pragmatic

   Ownership lies in the hands of the Product Manager", the PO "seems
   only to be responsible for driving and overseeing the execution";

   leadership fades away"; Perri — "I ha

- **Two roles split by facing (market/development) — Pragmatic, SAFe.**

# Verification review 2 — pm-po-one-role-2026-08 draft v2

Verifier: fresh context, 2026-08-25. Method: draft v2 read in full against review-1.md; every round-1 source reopened live this session (Milner via WebFetch; scrumguides.org/revisions.html; InfoQ Q&A; MDPI Remta & Buchalcevová 2021 via r.jina.ai; ISO 24765 PDF text (local extraction iso.txt, 3.2603); Mintzberg 1980 OCR (mintz.txt, "The Coordinating Mechanisms"); less.works product-owner page). Spot-check sources reopened live: Perri (via r.jina.ai), Pragmatic (both articles via r.jina.ai, curl + grep), Sverrisdottir abstract (Semantic Scholar API), Team Topologies key-concepts, Bass & Haxby PDF text, Koch & Wellbrock PDF text.

## (1) Round-1 repairs

1. Milner / role → accountabilities. Repaired. Summary item 3 now attributes the job-title reading to Milner's commentary with his hedge ("Apparently some people thought that the term 'role' meant job title" — verbatim on the Mountain Goat page) and states that the revisions page gives no rationale (confirmed: the 2020 notes list seven headings and mention "three different sets of accountabilities" without explaining the word change). "Precisely" is gone. One residual imprecision — see finding 1 below.
2. Remta & Buchalcevová Discussion vs Conclusions. Repaired. F4 bullet now labels "the removal of the Product Owner's real product ownership. In SAFe, the real Product Ownership lies in the hands of the Product Manager" as discussion (confirmed in Discussion) and quotes the Conclusions wording "the Product Manager has real product ownership, while the Product Owner is responsible for driving and overseeing the implementation of the requirements" (confirmed in Conclusions). The SAFe "single person cannot handle" sentence sits in Results 3.1.4; the draft calls it "quoting SAFe", which is accurate. "Literature mapping" is a fair description: the paper states it followed the Kitchenham et al. mapping process.
3. ISO 24765 definition 2 credit. Repaired. F3 and summary item 3 both say "definition 2, credited to the PMBOK Guide 4th ed."; iso.txt 3.2603 confirms three definitions, the second credited to "A Guide to the Project Management Body of Knowledge (PMBOK Guide) — Fourth Edition", wording verbatim.
4. Mintzberg "at least five basic ways". Repaired. F5 bullet now reads: structuring "focuses on the division of labor... and then the coordination of all of these tasks", which "can be effected in at least five basic ways". OCR lines 119–122 confirm both fragments verbatim; the "requires" gloss is gone.
5. F4/F5 heading labels. Repaired. F4: "(high that the sources say so; medium on the consequence)"; F5: "(high for the grounds; medium for Bass & Haxby's pattern)" — identical to the summary splits.
6. LeSS "fake PO" quote. Repaired. Only "She acts as a connector, not an intermediary" remains (verbatim on less.works). No "fake PO"/"interim" text anywhere in the draft.

## (2) Five further spot-checks (not named in round 1)

- Perri: "Product Owner is a role you play on a Scrum team. Product Manager is the job." — verbatim (source bolds "role" and "job"; draft drops the emphasis, acceptable). Confirmed.
- Pragmatic: "When everyone sits together, there's no need for a product owner" — verbatim; source continues "(or requirements analyst...)". "a product owner's responsibilities are just a small subset of product management" — verbatim. Both are in "The Strategic Role of Product Management (When Development Goes Agile)", not in "Product Owner vs Product Manager: What's the difference?"; the draft attributes to "Pragmatic Institute" generically and lists both articles in Sources. Confirmed; no change required.
- Sverrisdottir et al. 2014 abstract: "Cases were reported where there are two product owners for the same product. One is then responsible for business aspect but the other is responsible for technical aspects of the product." — verbatim; draft truncates after "technical aspects" without ellipsis, tolerable. Confirmed.
- Team Topologies: "Each new tool, responsibility or domain your team is given taxes their mental bandwidth." — verbatim. Confirmed.
- Bass & Haxby 2018: "Product sponsors surround themselves with a product owner team and delegate to a named product owner" and "the purpose of the intermediary is to be more accessible and available" — verbatim in bass.txt lines 91–99. Koch & Wellbrock anti-pattern row: "Human as liability buffer | Employees carry responsibility without time or authority | Give review time, criteria, override rights, and escalation paths." — verbatim in koch.txt lines 874–879 (the draft joins the three table cells with dashes, a faithful rendering). Confirmed.

## (3) Item 7's new sentence

"...it is a fact a general ask mechanism would serve on its own — an activity in any role that can hold its run and put a question to another role removes the need to encode 'who may ask the human' as a role boundary at all." This is reasoning from ground (c), not a sourced factual claim; it cites no source and asserts nothing about the sources. Document History attributes it to "the authority's observation on interaction", a reference to direction, not evidence. No confidence label, consistent with item 7's stated status as judgment. Acceptable.

## (4) Labels and banned words

- "seat" and "surface" do not appear (grep, case-insensitive; "likelihood" appears only in the scheme definition).
- No phrase combines confidence and likelihood; no likelihood phrase appears anywhere outside the scheme.
- F1, F2, F3 high: several sources opened in full with primaries — reproducible. F5 "medium for Bass & Haxby's pattern": one opened source — reproducible. F6 "medium — one paper opened in full, plus vendor guidance": one opened primary — reproducible. F4 / item 4 "medium on the consequence": not reproducible from the scheme — see finding 2.

verdict: findings

Both findings are labelling/attribution precision; no quote is fabricated or misworded, no source cited is unopened, nothing needs retraction.

1. Location: Executive summary item 3, clause "the Guide's own revisions page gives no rationale, and its authors cite removing the separate Development Team".
   At issue: read in sequence, "its authors cite removing the separate Development Team" presents the Development Team removal as the authors' rationale for the role → accountabilities change.
   What the sources say: the InfoQ Q&A contains no statement from Schwaber or Sutherland about why "roles" became "accountabilities". Schwaber's "The goal was to eliminate the concept of a separate team, the Development Team... could create 'us and them' behavior" explains the one-team change, not the word change. The revisions page likewise does not connect the two. Review-1 itself described InfoQ as giving "a different rationale", which the repair carried over as if it were a rationale for the same change.
   Required change: reword to make the referent explicit, e.g. "the Guide's own revisions page gives no rationale for the word change, and the authors' only stated rationale (InfoQ) concerns removing the separate Development Team". F2's Schwaber bullet is correctly scoped and needs no change.

2. Location: Executive summary item 4 and F4 heading, "medium on the consequence, which rests on case studies and practitioner report".
   At issue: the scheme defines medium as "one opened source, or secondary accounts only". The consequence claim rests on three sources opened in full (Remta & Buchalcevová 2021, Remta et al. 2020, Perri), two of them primary research; under the scheme as written that is high. The medium label is defensible on evidence strength (no controlled comparison — Verwijs), but that criterion is not in the scheme, so the label is not reproducible from it.
   Required change: either (a) add one clause to the scheme in the executive summary — e.g. "medium also where the agreeing sources are case studies or practitioner report with no controlled comparison" — leaving the labels as they are, or (b) relabel the consequence high and keep the caveat in the Limitations bullet. Option (a) preserves the report's intent; round 1 accepted the label without checking it against the scheme.

No other changes required.
